CME.note: Faint CME with a fuzzy front (multiple fronts) to the SW. A possible considered source could be a significant eruption near AR 3939 (S17W15) starting around 2025-01-01T00:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. While in SOHO the fuzzy front can be traced over multiple timestamps, in STEREO A COR2 a super faint front to the SW is seen only in two timestamps.

Measurement based on the potential source location of S17W15. At the time of the analysis, the source eruption from S15W77 was determined to be the more likely candidate for this CME, and the CME was simulated based on those parameters.

CME.note: Faint CME obscured by a pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 bc of a large data gap. The source could be minor activity from AR 3936 (N13W70) around 01Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain one-coronagraph analysis with SOHO coronagraph only based on the assumption that minor activity in Active Region 3936 is the source of this CME.

CME.note: Faint fast jet to the NW with the possible source a very minor eruption likely from AR 3934 (N13W81) near NW limb at 2024-12-31T23:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on a fit with two coronagraphs.

CME.note: Faint CME to the SSW, not seen in STEREO A because of a data gap from 2025-01-01T04:38Z to 2025-01-02T01:23Z. No clear source found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

CME.note: CME to the NW in SOHO, fully covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. Two potential sources are activity from from AR 3936 starting about 2025-01-01T10:36Z, a minor filament eruption from AR 3934 on the NW limb.

Faint CME first seen in the NE beginning at 2025-01-02T02:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 or SOHO LASCO C3 due to faintness. The source of this event is an area of brightening and field line movement seen along the NE limb (approx. N10E90) as seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. This CME fit with longitudes between -85 and -110.

CME.note: Narrow CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-02T03:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is field line movement tracing down to an unnumbered region located at approximately N20E60 as seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2

CME.note: Faint CME first seen in the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-02T03:36Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames before a data gap begins at 2025-01-02T04:38Z. This event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to faintness. The source of this event may be some minor field line movement seen along the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely related to the eruption from Active Region 13939 (S20W30) starting around 2025-01-02T14:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171, 195 and 284 imagery. Dimming is also observed around this time in GOES SUVI 195 imagery. This event overlaps with CME: 2025-01-02T15:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not possible. SHOCK measurement of the faint, outermost feature based on the source location. This measurement may vary as there is no STEREO A COR2 imagery to confirm the measured parameters. This measurement does not take into account possible deflection from the source location.

The source is likely related to the eruption from Active Region 13939 (S20W30) starting around 2025-01-02T14:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171, 195 and 284 imagery. Dimming is also observed around this time in GOES SUVI 195 imagery. This event overlaps with CME: 2025-01-02T15:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not possible. The measured parameters may vary slightly as this measurement does not take into account possible deflection from the source.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source is likely related to an M1.1 flare and eruption observed from Active Region 13939 (S10W30) starting around 2025-01-02T17:40Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 294, 304 imagery. Post eruptive brightening is observed in GOES SUVI 195 imagery starting around 2025-01-02T18:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not possible. The measured parameters may vary slightly as this measurement does not take into account possible deflection from the source.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source may be far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk that may be associated with this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the far-sided/unknown source location.

CME.note: Wide loop CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-03T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap beginning at 2025-01-03T11:09Z. The source of this CME is an X1.2 flare from AR 3947 (N10E64) peaking at 2025-01-03T11:39Z. This flare is seen clearly in GOES SUVI 94 and 131 imagery, along with field line movement visible in GOES SUVI 171, 195 and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. Measurement made with only early C2 frames due to ongoing SOHO and STEREO data gaps.

CME.note: Faint, narrow CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-03T15:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a minor eruption located at approx. S12E23 beginning at approx. 03/14:00Z. This eruption can be seen exhibiting a Southeastern deflection in GOES SUVI 195 and 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and is seen in STEREO A COR2 for a few frames following a data gap from 2025-01-03T18:23Z to 2025-01-04T01:23Z, before becoming too diffuse to observe. The source is related to an eruption and X1.1 flare from Active Region 13947 (N11E60) peaking at 2025-01-03T22:41Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284 imagery, and faint dimming is observed surrounding the eruption site in GOES SUVI 195 as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: Partial halo CME first visible to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-01-04T05:48Z. Also visible to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Some continuous outflow continues for a few hours after the start time of the CME. The source of this CME is likely far-sided. Some moving field lines beyond the WNW limb can been seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting about 2025-01-04T05:36Z. There is also some activity seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 from active region 3936, which was ~W116 at the time of eruption, at approximately 2025-01-04T05:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Measurements give a possible range in longitudes from ~W110 to ~W140.

CME.note: CME first visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-01-04T13:25Z. This CME is only visible for a couple faint frames in SOHO LASCO C3 and is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely an X1.8 flare from AR 3947 that peaked at 2025-01-04T12:48Z. The flare and some ejected material can be seen in GOES SUVI 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, and 304 starting around 2025-01-04T12:30Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on likely source location visible in GOES SUVI.

CME.note: CME associated with a long duration C9.3-class flare near the vicinity of AR 3939 (S17W55) that begins at approximately 2025-01-04T14:30Z, seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. It can be seen across all GOES SUVI wavelengths, but is particularly prominent in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft measurement since there is no STEREO A COR2 imagery. Measurement based on source candidate from GOES SUVI.

CME.note: Fast partial halo seen generally to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 quickly leaving the SOHO C2 field of view, seemingly associated with an eruption from near the vicinity of Active Region 3939 (S17W58) and associated long duration C7.6-class flare. Quickly moving field lines off the west limb and bright post eruptive arcades are observed in GOES SUVI 284/304. Associated with solar energetic particle events at SOHO, GOES, and STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement with no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for triangulation, assuming that the eruption is indeed on the Earth facing disk and associated with Active Region 3939 near W58.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: Very faint and quick to fade CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-05T10:12Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2 due to its faintness. The source of this event is an M4.1 flare from AR 3947 (N12E41) peaking at 05/09:36Z. This flare is visible in GOES SUVI 131 and post eruptive arcades can be seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. This event fades after only a few frames and will therefore not be simulated.

CME.note: Faint CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-05T16:36Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2 due to faintness and a fading front. The source of this event is an M2.4 flare from AR 3947 (N12E40) peaking at 05/15:47Z. This flare can be seen in GOES SUVI 131 along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. This CME fades after a few frames before exiting the FOV in SOHO LASCO C2 and will therefore not be simulated.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-05T20:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a minor eruption from AR 3947 (N15E35) seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

The source of this CME is most likely an M4.8 flare from AR 3947 (N15E26) that peaked at 2025-01-06T17:24Z. The flare and eruption can be seen in GOES SUVI 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, and 304. A subsequent EUV wave can be seen with slight eastward deflection in GOES SUVI 195 and 284. Another source possibility is a small amount of ejecta from behind the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-01-06T16:08Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement is based on probable source location identified from GOES SUVI imagery. The leading edge is only well-defined enough to measure for four frames in SOHO LASCO C2, so there is quite of bit of uncertainty in this measurement.

CME.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-01-06T20:00Z. Also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some activity from on or beyond the W limb. There are some opening field lines from beyond the limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting about 2025-01-06T18:28Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement is based on probable source location identified in GOES SUVI and on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-01-06T23:00Z. Also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely a minor C2.7 flare peaking at 2025-01-06T22:10Z from AR 3941 (S06W79) and some accompanying ejecta best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-01-06T22:04Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable source location identified in GOES SUVI and on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs.

CME.note: Super faint CME to the S (SE in STEREO A). The source could be a C2.5 flare and a minor eruption near AR 3951 (S14W06) seen after 09:35Z as dimming/brightening in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source is likely a slowly developing filament eruption visible near the southwest limb spanning S60W60 to S37W75 (centered around S50W70) which begins to erupt around 2025-01-07T15:30Z, seen best in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. A gradual opening field lines are visible in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 imagery around this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not possible. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

CME.note: Asymmetrical loop CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. This CME is partially obstructed by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 which lasted from 2025-01-07T17:53Z to 2025-01-08T01:38Z. Source is a large eruption and brightening associated with the long-duration M1.1 flare located just beyond SW limb, likely from AR 3939 (S17W99), as seen in GOES SUVI. Widely opening field lines, brightening, and ejection of material can be seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/211/304 starting at about 2025-01-07T22:10Z. The tops of post-eruptive arcades can be seen emerging from beyond the SW limb in GOES SUVI 171 starting at about 2025-01-07T23:48Z. There is some uncertainty in the exact location of this eruption since this is not directly on the disk, but it is very likely associated with Active Region 13939 which is estimated to have been located at roughly S17W99 at the peak time of the flare [2025-01-07T23:05Z].

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery and source location (S17W99) based on UV imagery.

A subsequent faint opening of field lines is visible over the western limb around this time in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284 imagery, and post-eruptive arcades begin to form around 2025-01-08T02:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a faint and slow opening of field lines visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 171 imagery starting around 2025-01-08T02:00Z, possibly associated with a faint eruption centered near N45E45 at this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided, and may be related to faint field line movement visible over the western limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2025-01-08T04:50Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

N20E100) as seen in SDO AIA 193, followed by intense post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 131 and 193 from the same area. This suggests a possible far sided eruption.

A possible source for this CME is a minor eruption seen along the SE limb (approx. S15E85) in SDO AIA 304 beginning at approx. 10/09:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2

CME.note: Flux rope CME first seen very faintly in SOHO LASCO C2 and becomes increasingly more visible in C3 and COR2A. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery.

CME.note: Diffuse and relatively narrow CME to the N/NW first seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, then shortly thereafter in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Source is an eruption near the NW limb at N24W80 with narrowly opening field lines and ejecta seen starting at 2025-01-11T07:58Z in GOES SUVI 195/131/171/284 and a small rising loop of filamentary material seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-01-11T07:57Z, all wavelengths showing heavy northern deflection. This eruption is associated with a C2.8 flare with peak time 2025-01-11T08:44Z produced by simultaneous brightening from recently-decayed AR 13954 (N24W76) as well as an unnumbered region just beyond the E limb located at an estimated N19E90-N19E100.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery. Some uncertainty due to extreme faintness of leading edge in STEREO A COR2 difference imagery and use of reduced-cadence frames in C3 due to comet campaign.

CME.note: Faint jet with a fuzzy, quickly disappearing front, seen in SOHO LASCO and in only one timestamp of STEREO A COR2 after a data gap. The source could be some very minor flaring and minor eruptions close to the W limb seen in AIA 193 around 21:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: The front of this CME is not really clear in COR2 (after the gap), so a POS measurement is the best we can do.

CME.note: Narrow CME visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The potential source location can be seen on the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 195/304 as an ejecta of material and opening field lines starting around 2025-01-12T04:05Z. It is also visible beyond the limb in GOES SUVI 171/195/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

CME.note: Very faint narrow CME with fuzzy (not clear) front seen in several  timestamps of SOHO LASCO C2 and at least one timestamp in STEREO A COR2, with clear front not seen in C3 imagery. A possible source could be a minor filament eruption close to NW limb seen in AIA 304 starting at 19:19Z.

Minor faint and narrow jet with a fuzzy front mostly seen in C2 and one timestamp of COR2A, covered by pylon in C3. Its source possibly a very minor filament eruption in AIA 304 around 4:30Z behind the NW limb or a very minor activity in AR 3947 (N11W68) in AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit of the very fuzzy, unclear front with two coronagraphs.

CME.note: Faint high latitude CME, covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely the narrow filament eruption close to/off the NW limb (N25W90) seen around 2025-01-13T14:08Z in SDO AIA 304. It looks like the source is likely on the limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: One-coronagraph analysis based on the possible source location on the NW limb.

CME.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is related to a filament eruption centered near S35W45 which begins to erupt around 2025-01-13T23:50Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: Fast, thin CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. This CME is directed straight into the C3 pylon, which made it difficult to track the precise front beyond C2 and COR2A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: Fast, thin CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source appears to be on/just beyond the NW limb around N16, as field line movement and thin filament ejecta deflecting northward from this area beginning around 2025-01-14T08:48Z in SDO AIA 171/195/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. This CME is directed straight into the C3 pylon, which made it difficult to track the precise front beyond C2 and COR2A.

The source is likely far-sided, and may be related to a small eruption visible on/near the northeast limb starting around 2025-01-15T17:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 and 304 imagery. A faint opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the uncertain source location and data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS analysis is the only analysis possible, since the source is behind the limb and no STEREO A COR2 imagery is available.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location and best fit in only SOHO LASCO C3. Not captured in STEREO A COR2 in real time; data gap in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2025-01-25T18:23Z.

CME.note: Faint, wide CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and NE in STEREO COR2A. No source observed on the disk for this event, but it triangulates between coronagraphs to around N34W02. This CME begins to incredibly slowly evolve to the N as early as 2025-01-25T06:00Z, with brighter material slowly emerging around 2025-01-25T20:48Z that accelerates in later frames of SOHO LASCO C3 to its final speed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A. Only uses later frames of SOHO LASCO C3 due to acceleration from earlier C3 frames and C2.

CME.note: CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 (for all frames) and STEREO COR2A (starting at 2025-01-26T02:23Z when a data gap ends). Source is a filament eruption in the southeast quadrant of the Earth-facing disk, with liftoff starting around 2025-01-26T00:08Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. The curved filament occupied an oval-shaped area on the disk spanning S10-S30 and E38-E65 just prior to eruption. Filamentary material and post eruptive brightening can be seen in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-01-25T00:45Z. Post-eruptive arcades become visible in SDO AIA 171/193/131 around 2025-01-26T02:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SHOCK measurement of the faint, shock-like feature extending much wider than the brighter bulk, best observed in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. Only two usable frames of STEREO COR2A are available to triangulate this feature, and its longitude could range E40-E60 around the eruption source at E51.
BULK measurement of the brighter, inner feature of this CME. Triangulates well between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery near the observed source centered around S20E51.

CME.note: Narrow CME with the source the same location as the filament eruption producing 2025-01-26T01:25Z CME. This time it is a minor eruption seen around 2025-01-26T10:10Z near ~S20E55 in AIA 304, with brightening and post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fits with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the source eruption.

CME.note: Faint CME seen in SOHO LASCO only (b/c of data gap in STEREO A coronagraph imagery). Source is another (but more minor) eruption in the SE quadrant starting around 18:41Z and centered around ~(S23E48), as seen in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 304/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: One coronagraph analysis with SOHO LASCO imagery only, based on the clear location of the source eruption. There are no STEREO A coronagraph images available at this point because of the daily gap.

CME.note: CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and in STEREO COR2A starting at 2025-01-27T02:23Z returning from a data gap. The source for this CME is likely narrow filament ejecta from AR 3961 around 2025-01-27T23:28 in SDO AIA 304, located on the west limb around S10W90 at this time. Weak field line movement on/near the NW limb near cluster of ARs 3971/3965/3962, best observed in GOES SUVI 171 around 2025-01-27T23:25Z, creates a diffuse overlapping coronagraph signature to the NW of this more clear signature traveling SW.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement at W90 for the observed source in SDO AIA imagery, not a plane of sky. Triangulates between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery, though notably faint and tought to discern in STEREO COR2A beacon running difference imagery.

CME.note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is observed on/just beyond the SW limb as filament ejecta visible in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 starting at 2025-01-27T00:15Z, and is likely AR 3961 (S10W90 at time of eruption).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. Due to poor visibility of this CME in STEREO COR2A running difference imagery, and the known source at W90 in SDO imagery, this longitude could slightly range W75-W95.

CME.note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-27T11:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament ejection beginning at 2025-01-27T10:32Z seen just around the SW limb in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-27T16:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2025-01-27T15:38Z. The source of this CME is field line movement and dimming seen near AR 3972 (S19W57) in SDO AIA 171 and 193 beginning at 2025-01-27T14:54Z. The dimming expands to the South of the Active Region suggesting a Southern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Due to the bizarre shape of this CME, especially in SOHO LASCO C2, this measurement was based on the furthest edge seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and more defined shape seen in SOHO LASCO C3

CME.note: CME first seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-27T17:36Z. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2A due to a data gap beginning at 2025-01-27T15:38Z, and fades before entering the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this event is field line movement seen along the South limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 beginning at 2025-01-27T16:59Z, suggesting a far sided source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2

CME.note: Faint loop CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and SW in STEREO A COR2. Source is an eruption from AR 13961 (S10, approx. W105-110) just beyond the SW limb. Brightening is seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery at S10W110 (coordinates from perspective of Earth-facing disk) at 2025-01-28T08:05Z. Opening field lines are seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 starting at 2025-01-28T08:05Z, and the absence of post-eruptive arcades and/or dimming on the Earth-facing disk further suggests this eruption is beyond the SW limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using location of source observed in UV imagery and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Leading edge is very faint, especially in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

CME.note: CME first seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-01-28T20:12Z. CME is also seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C3 and is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is possibly a small eruption from near the E limb (~S07).

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Due to the lack of a definitive source, there is low confidence in this measurement.

Updated measurement based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

CME.note: Faint CME to the SW with the source the minor opening of field lines on/likely behind the SW limb starting at 2025-01-29T18:33Z as seen in AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS analysis based on SOHO imagery only. At the moment STEREO A coronagraph imagery is not available.
Approximated longitude based on source location. Plausible longitude fits range from approx. W90 to W125.

CME.note: CME first seen in the SW by STEREO A COR2, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a data gap from 30/04:00Z to 30/07:36Z. The source of this CME is field line movement seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284, suggesting a far sided source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

CME.note: Faint CME first seen to the SW beginning at 2025-01-30T09:12Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This event is overtaken by CME: 2025-01-30T11:12Z in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is rising field line loops seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2A. This event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 as it overlaps with CME: 2025-01-30T11:12Z.

CME.note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-01-30T11:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is field line opening seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171, 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195, indicating a far sided source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2
SHOCK measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

CME.note: Flux rope CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. CME not captured by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which started at 2025-01-30T15:09Z. The source is a filament eruption seen beginning at approx. 2025-01-30T13:49Z in SDO AIA 304, spanning approx. S05E05 to S40E40. Dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on central location of filament eruption as seen in UV imagery, and best fit of shape in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 frames. CME not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-01-30T15:09Z.

CME.note: Faint partial-halo CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, which remains visible into the C3 field of view. Overlaps with CME:2025-01-30T16:12Z, which is much more well-defined in coronagraph imagery. This CME is not captured by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which started at 2025-01-30T15:09Z. The source of this CME is a distinct set of opening field lines and post-eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 94/171/193 around 2025-01-30T14:25Z located at approx. S15E10, as part of the same filament eruption which sourced CME:2025-01-30T16:12Z, which was seen beginning at approx. 2025-01-30T13:49Z in SDO AIA 304, spanning approx. S05E05 to S40E40.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on location of opening field lines and brightest portion of post-eruptive arcades associated with an elongated filament eruption as seen in UV imagery, and best fit of shape in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 frames. This CME was not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-01-30T15:09Z.

CME.note: Loop CME seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. This CME is not captured by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which started at 2025-01-30T15:09Z. The source of thus event is field line opening seen along/from just beyond the Western limb starting at 2025-01-30T17:57Z in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement taken, since source seen in UV imagery indicated that the eruption was beyond the W limb, and COR2A was not available in real time. CME not captured in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-01-30T15:09Z.
